Roblox claims to have made changes to its hugely popular children's app to protect children from predators, but regulators say these protections are not enough.

The regulator found four major shortcomings, including the ability for adults to send friend requests to children without parental approval...

Australia's eSafety Commissioner has today compiled the vulnerabilities found during testing:

  • Adults can send friend requests to Australian children without parental or guardian consent;
  • Children and adults can view and respond to each other's posts on forums outside the gaming environment without parental or guardian consent;
  • A child's friend list is visible to anyone on the Roblox platform;
  • A child's profile and bio, including account name, number of friends and their names, avatar image, and non-sensitive personal profile information such as interests, are visible to anyone on the Roblox platform, with no ability to restrict the visibility of this information.

The regulator said Roblox has agreed to implement stricter measures within three months:

  • Preventing adults from contacting unknown children without parental consent
  • Strengthening children's account settings so they default to private
  • Providing an easy-to-use reporting mechanism and notifying users of complaint outcomes
  • Hiring an independent third-party audit firm to assess the effectiveness of its safety measures, including the deployment of age estimation measures

Roblox has more than 380 million active users, the majority of whom are under 16.
